evidence.reply_text: The try block contains code that may raise an exception; if an exception occurs, the rest of the try is skipped and Python jumps to the first except clause that matches, and after handling it execution continues after the whole try‑except‑else‑finally construct. The else clause runs only if no exception was raised, the finally clause always runs even when a return occurs, and when two except clauses could both match, the later one in the source is chosen.

evidence.reason: The candidate explicitly states that the later clause is chosen when two except clauses match, which reflects a misunderstanding of how Python evaluates except blocks (top-to-bottom vs specificity/later order).
